en: The Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva Heart Mantra Sūtra, also known as the Tārā Heart Sūtra, translated by the Śramaṇa Shi Zhitong of Zongchi Monastery during the Great Tang Dynasty by imperial decree.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was staying at Vulture Peak Mountain in the great city of Rājagṛha.
He was accompanied by an immeasurable number of great bhikṣus,
as well as immeasurable devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras,
each together with their retinues.
Furthermore, he was surrounded by an immeasurable and incalculable number of bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās, who paid him their respects.
At that time, there was a bodhisattva within the assembly.
Named Avalokiteśvara, he immediately rose from his seat, prostrated at the Buddha’s feet,
bared his right shoulder, and knelt with his right knee on the ground.
With palms joined in reverence, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, I now wish to expound the root mantra and the methods for the mudrās and maṇḍalas of the *Aritori* Heart-Mantra.
The power of this mantra is inconceivable."
It brings peace and happiness to the world and provides manifold benefit.
If there are devas or humans who uphold it,
all their adversaries, evil obstacles, and fears will [be dispelled].
All [malevolent influences] will be completely stilled;
all the prohibitions and incantations of non-Buddhist practitioners will be shattered and dispersed, unable to cause harm.
All virtuous deeds shall be accomplished according to one’s wishes.
Among all sentient beings, whether four-footed or two-footed, there are none who do not show reverence; they shall all submit and take refuge.
I only pray that the World-Honored One will compassionately grant his hearing and permission.
Out of great compassion and pity for all sentient beings,
I shall now expound this method of the Root Seal Mantra— that is, the method of the Mūla-dhāraṇī.

1. The Mantra of the随心印 (Sui-xin-yin), Chapter One. It is also called the 身印呪 (Shen-yin-zhou) and the 都印呪 (Du-yin-zhou). With both hands, [place] the three fingers—the middle, ring, and little fingers—[together].
Interlace the fingers outward;
join the palms with the right hand placed over the left,
and clench the tips of the fingers together against the back of the palms.
Extend both index fingers so that they touch each other;
do the same with the thumbs,
each grasping its respective index finger.
Moving the thumb back and forth,
he then spoke the mantra: *Namo hradanātrāya* (1) *namo 'ri*.
Jaya-vāruṇi-jiteśvara | Bodhisattva | Mahāsattva | Mahākāruṇika | Tadyathā | Oṃ | Tare | Tare | Tuttare | Tuttare ||
10. *Tuḥre svāhā*. 11. Second: The Incantation for Invoking.
Using the Body Seal (*kāyamudrā*), recite this incantation:
*Tadyathā*: 1. *Āgaccha āgaccha*, 2. *bhagavan*, 3. *ariye*, 4. *varakīte*, 5. *śabara*.
*Yarātana-tara-satena svāhā.* Recite this mantra seven times over agallochum incense and burn it.
When one requests the Bodhisattva, he will come.
If you wish to recite the aforementioned Tārā Heart Mantra,
first recite this mantra seven times, and only then recite the former.

3. The Seal and Mantra for Invocation. This third section on the seal and mantra for invocation applies universally to all Bodhisattvas. With the right hand extended forward, grasp the wrist of the left hand.
Move the four fingers of the left hand back and forth over the head.
Then recite the mantra:
Oṃ sarvabodhisattvanayane nayane svāhā. (4) The Mantra of the Flower-Pedestal Seal (Puṣkara-pīṭha-mudrā). This fourth seal is performed according to the previous method.
Only change the palms so that both hands face upward,
with each of the five fingers slightly bent upward.
The mantra says:
Oṃ sarvapraṇiṣṭha buddhānā svāhā. (5) The fifth is the incense and flower mudrā mantra. With the thumb of the right hand...
Press the ring finger against the nail of the thumb;
extend the remaining three fingers straight.
Then, support the underside of the right hand with the palm of the left hand.
The mantra is:
Oṃ sarvabodhya puṣpagaye svāhā. When performing this rite, the eight classes of devas and nāgas will be moved to come and make offerings.
6. The Mudrā and Dhāraṇī of Fragrant Water, Chapter Six: With the middle, ring, and little fingers of both hands, clench them like fists so that each grasps its own thumb.
Join the wrists and touch the two index fingers together.

The mantra is: Oṃ sarvabuddhāgrya rāja svāhā. This mudrā is used for making offerings to all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges. The Seventh: The Mantra of the Body-Protection Mudrā. First, join the palms.
Bend the two small fingernails so that they face each other.
Place the two thumbs against the two index fingers.
Join the tips of the remaining three fingers and touch them together.
Open the palms slightly and move the index fingers back and forth above the crown of the head.
The mantra is as follows:

*Tadyathā:* (1) *ari*, (2) *tari*, (3) *dutari*, (4) *duri*, (5) *he raṇa-rye*, (6) *garbhi*, (7) *harākṣa harākṣama-ja* [here one should utter one's own name], (8) *sarvaduḥkha-priye*, (9) *bodhisattva-pratibhaye*, (10) *svāhā*. Recite this mantra while forming this mudrā one hundred thousand times.
All Māras, followers of external paths, humans,
non-humans, and the like shall have no power to cause harm;
one should employ this for the protection of the body.
Furthermore, forming this mudrā and reciting the aforementioned mantra,
one should, before a śarīra stūpa,
with a sincere heart, confess and repent for all transgressions.
It can extinguish the sins of the four grave offenses, the five heinous acts, and so forth.
8. The Heart-Seal Mantra (Citta-mudrā-dhāraṇī), Eighth: This follows the previous body-protection seal;
the only change is that the two index fingers are used to pinch the two thumbs, with the tips of the nails touching one another.
Place it upon the heart.
The mantra is:
Oṃ sarvakhidhāya buddhāya svāhā. Having formed this mudrā, recite the heart-mantra at that time.
It is fully capable of eliminating all the various sins of the three karmas.
9. The Oral Seal Mantra (Mukhamudrā-mantra), the ninth: This follows the previous heart seal;
one simply changes it by using the two thumbs.
Bend [the fingers] toward the palms so that they both rest upon the joints of the two little fingers.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ vibhavaśikāye svāhā. Having formed this mudrā, when reciting the oral mantra, one is able to eliminate all karmic obstacles of verbal action.
10. The Seal and Mantra of the Great Repentance (Mahā-deśanā-mudrā-mantra), Number Ten. First, with the right hand, press the tip of the middle finger’s nail with the thumb;
extend the remaining three fingers straight.
The left hand is likewise;
with the right thumb, press upon the nail of the left thumb.
Place it directly before the heart.
The mantra is:
Oṃ sarvabuddhabodhisattvāya svāhā. Recite this mantra while performing repentance.
This is capable of removing all karmic obstacles and other transgressions. 11.

The Seal and Mantra for Summoning All Mighty Ghosts, Spirits, Devas, Nāgas, and the Eight Divisions. The eleventh [chapter]: The Seal and Mantra for Summoning All Mighty Ghosts, Spirits, Devas, Nāgas, and the Eight Divisions. With the right hand, one presses upon the back of the left hand.
Interlace the four fingers of both hands with the palms facing downward.
Move the four fingers of the left hand back and forth.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ krodha sarvadevanā svāhā. (12) The Great Boundary-Sealing Mantra for Expelling Vināyakas, Number Twelve. First, with the ring finger of the right hand...
Insert [the right hand] into the back of the ring finger of the left hand;
with the thumb of the left hand,
hook and grasp the little finger of the right hand.
With the right hand placed palm-upward,
use the index, middle, and ring fingers of the left hand to hook the middle finger of the right hand.
Press both hands together with the right ring finger resting upon the nail of the left ring finger; then,
touch the tips of the right index finger and the left little finger to one another.
With the right hand, place the thumb over the backs of the left index and middle fingers and twist the left wrist;
the mantra is as follows:
Oṃ (1) sarvayakṣa (2) rākṣasānāṃ (3) bandha bandha (4) svāhā (5). When this seal and mantra are performed, all ghosts and spirits will naturally submit and be subdued.
13. The Seal of Following the Mind, Number Thirteen. This follows the previous seal for delimiting the boundary (*sīmābandha*).
The only modification is that the index finger of the right hand and the little finger of the left hand are separated by a distance of about one inch.
This is called the Seal that Follows the Mind. Having formed this seal, recite the Mantra of the Body that Follows the Mind;
all that is wished for shall be attained. 14.

The Seal for Entering the Path and Begging Alms to Deliver the Māra Pāpīyān. Regarding the Fourteenth Seal for Entering the Path and Begging Alms to Deliver the Māra Pāpīyān: first, take the middle and ring fingers of the right hand.
Curl the index finger so it rests within the palm;
keep the remaining three fingers straight and upright;
then extend the palm outward toward the chest.
The left hand is likewise;
with the palm facing outward, it supports [the other].
When performing this mudrā:
The Māra Pāpīyān, leading his retinue,
aspired to enter the Buddha-way, prostrated himself, and withdrew while reciting the Body Dharani.
15. The Seal for Subduing the Six Heretical Teachers. Regarding the Seal for Subduing the Six Heretical Teachers, the fifteenth:
it is according to the previous seal, with the only modification being that each [finger] uses the thumb.
Press the tips of the ring fingers and middle fingers together.
When this mudrā is formed,
the six heretical teachers will all submit and be subdued.
Recite the Body Mantra. 16.

The Seal and Mantra for Saving Sentient Beings Seen in the Six Realms and Causing Them to Leave Suffering and Attain Liberation. For this sixteenth seal and mantra, join the two thumbs and the two index fingers of both hands together.
The two middle fingers are placed side by side with their tips touching.
The two ring fingers each press down upon the nails of the two little fingers,
leaving a space between them.
Place it upon the forehead.
The mantra is:
Oṃ sarvacakṣudhāra karaye svāhā. This is the body-mantra which the Master himself recites.
17. The Seventeenth [Mudrā]: Bestowing the Ambrosia Seal (Amṛta-mudrā).
With the left hand, join the index finger with the thumb;
extend the remaining three fingers straight upward, pointing outward.
Furthermore, with the right hand, let the arm hang downward;
extend the five fingers straight down.
Performing this, one executes the rite of bestowing nectar (*amṛta*).
May all sentient beings of the six realms be fully satisfied, freed from suffering, and liberated.
Recite the Body Mantra.
18. The Seal and Mantra for Averting Difficulties, Number Eighteen: With the right thumb...
Cross the right ribs with the fingertips pointing backward;
clench the remaining four fingers into a fist.
Do the same with the left hand.
Extend the arms forward and recite the mantra:
Oṃ sarvatusthāna cchinda cchinda svāhā. When performing this rite of mudrā and mantra, [one should do so].
To subdue all celestial Māras who are difficult to conquer, so that they all submit and none dare to oppose him. 19.
The Nineteenth Mantra of the Seal of Sovereignty (*Svairatāmudrā*). With the four fingers of both hands, cross them back-to-back.
Furthermore, touch the two index fingers together;
place the two thumbs apart and hold them upright, pointing upward.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ sarvabuddhadhāraya māraya svāhā. 20. The Samādhi Seal: Sit upright in the full lotus posture.
Place the palm of the left hand over the back of the right hand, pressing them together at the heart;
recite the Body Mantra and immediately enter the meditative absorption of cessation (*nirodhasamāpatti*).
21. The Mudrā and Dhāraṇī for Summoning King Yama. Second and Twenty-first: Interlock the two little fingers with their tips facing inward, pressing the right over the left.
Bend the two middle fingers and the two ring fingers so that each presses upon the nail of its respective thumb;
extend the two index fingers vertically, keeping them approximately five inches apart.
Move the index finger back and forth.
The mantra is:
Oṃ sarvayamarāja dvipiya svāhā. If one wishes to know the number of sentient beings in the hells or to inquire after their names:
The King himself led his generals and officials in attendance, coming personally to report to the practitioner. 22.
The Seal and Mantra for Summoning the Four Heavenly Kings (Caturmahārājika-saṃcodana-mudrā-mantra), Number Twenty-Two: With both hands, turn the four fingers inward and interlace them.
Bend both thumbs into the palms so that the tips of the fingers are concealed within;
move the fingertips back and forth.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ sarvadevakāraṇa svāhā. When one performs this mudrā and mantra while departing, the Four Great Heavenly Kings will all arrive simultaneously.
The practitioners each asked about matters concerning the four continents, and [the deity] informed them of all of them. 23.
The Seal and Mantra of Upholding the Precepts (Śīla-mudrā-mantra), Part Twenty-Three. Kneel with the right knee on the ground.
Raising the head upward,
place the palms together at the heart;
then, using the two index fingers...
Press the first phalanges on the dorsal side of the middle fingers;
place each of the two thumbs against the sides of the two index fingers.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ sarvapāramitāmukha khidraya svāhā. When forming this mudrā and reciting this mantra:
Innumerable beings of various classes attain the pure precepts. 24.
The Seal-Mantra for Concealing the Body and Entering the Six Realms According to Form, Part Twenty-Four. With the thumb of the right hand.
Press [the thumb] upon the middle nail of the ring finger;
extend the index and little fingers straight upward.
The left hand is likewise.
With the thumb of the right hand,
starting from below the left hand,
move it upward into the left palm.
Hook the middle and ring fingers of the left hand;
the right hand presses down upon the left.
The mantra says:
Oṃ kiliye svāhā. When performing this mudrā-rite, one may vanish at will and travel with complete mastery.
All shall be as wished. 25.
The Seal and Mantra for Summoning the Rishis Possessing the Five Supernatural Powers, etc., Part Twenty-Five. With the middle, ring, and little fingers of both hands.
Form fists with both hands joined together;
place each of the two thumbs against the side of the middle finger,
and move the index fingers back and forth.
The mantra is:
Oṃ sarvakṛtyā-karmapralāna-gotraye svāhā. When performing this ritual of mudrā, [recite it].
All the rishis were summoned and arrived together.
He questioned them regarding their methods of cultivation, and each explained them in full detail.
26. The Consecration Purification Seal Mantra. The twenty-sixth, the Consecration Purification Seal Mantra, follows the previous Five Supernormal Powers Seal.
In the former [mudrā], one simply changes it so that the index fingers are used;
each presses against the tip of the thumb, with the tips of the index fingers touching one another.
Furthermore, the two middle fingers are held upright, their tips touching.
Place it upon the crown of the head.
The mantra is:
Oṃ tikeṇava mūdrā saṃkha svāhā. If the practitioner has already established the great maṇḍala site, [he should proceed].
By using this dharma-seal to recite the mantra and perform the consecration (*abhiṣeka*), boundless sentient beings shall all attain purity. 27.
The Seal and Mantra for Water Dangers (*udaka-vighna-mudrā-mantra*). Twenty-seventh: First, take the middle fingers and ring fingers of both hands.
Interlace the hands so that the right presses down upon the left;
extend the two index fingers and the two little fingers straight upward with their tips touching one another;
and bend the two thumbs inward into the palms.
The mantra is:
Oṃ uttara sarvabhaya uttara svāhā. By performing this mudrā-rite, one cannot be swept away by water.
All the water deities submit and are brought under control. 28.
The Seal for Fire Calamity (Agni-āpad-mudrā), Number Twenty-Eight. This follows the previous seal for water calamity;
the only difference is that the two index fingers and the two little fingers are modified.
Each [finger] should be spaced about one cun apart.
Recite the *nāga-mantra* while using water.
One who performs this mudrā method cannot be burned by fire.
All the fire deities submit and are brought under control. 29.
The Seal for the Peril of Wind (Vāta-vighna-mudrā), Number Twenty-nine: First, using the middle and ring fingers of the right hand.
Interlace the fingers so that they enter behind the ring fingers of the left hand;
the two index fingers and the two little fingers follow suit.
Press the ring fingers and middle fingers of the left hand against the heart.
With the index and little fingers of the right hand,
press down upon the backs of the middle and ring fingers;
extend the two thumbs so that they are parallel and held upright with a space between them.
Turn the palms outward.
Perform the water-difficult mantra while forming this mudrā.
No calamities of wind can cause harm;
the kings of wind and rain deities all submit and take refuge. 30.
The Seal for Overcoming Heavenly Calamities (Din-nan-yin), Number Thirty. First, with the right hand, place the tips of the thumb and index finger together.
Press the second joint of the left index finger with [the right thumb].
Then, using the left index finger and thumb,
press the first joint of the right thumb.
The remaining three fingers are held upright with their tips touching one another,
each separated by approximately one cun;
for the mantra, use the body-mantra.
When forming this mudrā,
one shall behold the affairs of the Heaven of the Thirty-three,
and all celestial deities will completely submit and take refuge.
31. The Seal and Mantra for Earth Difficulties (Bhūmi-vighna-mudrā-mantra), Number Thirty-One. This is the same as the previous seal for earth difficulties;
the only change is that the two ring fingers are bent flat with their tips touching one another.
The mantra is:
Oṃ ghaṭaṅga hasitāye svāhā. When this seal-method is performed, all earth deities will completely submit and be subdued.
32. The Seal and Mantra for Difficulties Caused by Bandits, Number Thirty-Two: With the index, middle, ring, and little fingers of the right hand, hook the four fingers of the left hand.
The two thumbs are each spread apart and held straight up.
The mantra is: Oṃ sarvatusthāna cchindaya svāhā. When forming this mudrā:
All dangers from bandits shall be naturally bound so that they cannot cause harm.
33. The Seal-Mantra for Royal Perils (Rājan-mudrā-mantra), Number Thirty-Three. This follows the previous seal for dangers from bandits.
Above, only change it so that the right thumb hooks and grasps the left thumb;
then recite the mantra as follows:
Oṃ sarvarājatuṣṭāna svāhā. When performing this ritual with the mudrā, all kings, difficulties, instruments of suffering, swords, staves, and the like cannot cause harm.
34. The Third and Fourth: The Mantra of the Abhaya-mudrā (Seal of Fearlessness), also known as the Seal-mantra for Removing Terrors. Standing up, extend the left arm straight downward.
The five fingers are also extended downward,
with the palms and backs facing rearward;
the right hand is likewise.
With the palm facing forward,
perform the mudrā of the right hand as if bestowing nectar.
The mantra is as follows:
*Tadyathā:* Āli, dāli, tudāli, duli, hiraṇyagarbhe, rākṣa rākṣama-ja (here insert one's own name), sarvatucchibha, sarvatādrāvibha, svāhā. Recite this mantra one hundred thousand times.
When forming this seal, all sentient beings who possess fear shall attain fearlessness. The ancient manuscript lacks the mantra; it is present in the current edition. 35.

The Mantra for Sealing Protection Against Poisonous Difficulties. For the Mantra for Sealing Protection Against Poisonous Difficulties, number thirty-five: cross the four fingers of both hands with the backs facing each other.
Place the tips of the two thumbs together,
with the palms turned outward.
The mantra says:
Oṃ parākṣayeṇa bandha bandha svāhā. When one enters a mountain valley and performs this mudrā and mantra, [the obstacles will be bound].
All venomous snakes, tigers, wolves, lions,
and various poisonous birds and beasts cannot harm them;
nor can any other poisons cause them injury.
36. The Mantra for Seeking the Seal of Intelligence (The Thirty-sixth Mantra for Seeking the Seal of Intelligence).
With the thumbs of both hands, each press upon the upper joints of the two ring fingers.
The two little fingers are held side-by-side, straight, and upright, with their tips touching.
The sides of the heads of the two middle fingers are pressed together.
The two index fingers are bent so that each rests upon the second phalanx of its respective middle finger.
With the fingertips separated by about one inch,
form this mudrā directly before the heart while reciting the body-mantra.
If there are those of dull faculties:
If one performs this seal-offering (*mudrā-pūjā*) while seeking a boon, one’s wishes will be fulfilled as desired.
For those of dull faculties, perform it for seven days.
Long ago, in the kingdom of Sphatika, there was an elder.
Although his family was very wealthy, he was by nature dull-witted.
His teacher made offerings and sought blessings for him according to the Dharma for seven days;
consequently, he became intelligent and could recite a thousand verses daily.
The remaining proofs will not be recounted in full here. 37.
The Seal for Shattering Hell (Bhūmipātana-mudrā), the Thirty-seventh: With the two middle fingers and the two ring fingers of both hands...
Place each [hand] with the palms facing inward and the backs touching.
With the two thumbs, index fingers, and little fingers,
keep them each about half an inch apart while reciting the Body Mantra.
When this mudrā is formed,
the gates of hell open and sentient beings suffering there are simultaneously liberated;
King Yama conceives a heart of joy.
Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, out of great kindness, great compassion, and pity for sentient beings, has taught this dharma.
38. The Seal for Seeking Rebirth in the Pure Land (Third-Eight). Joining the palms at the heart.
Placing the two thumbs side by side upon the heart, recite the body-mantra while forming this mudrā;
with single-minded concentration, recite the mantra, and you will be reborn in whichever Buddha-land you desire according to your wish.
39. The Seal for Saving All Sentient Beings from the Suffering of Illness, Number Thirty-Nine:
With the two index fingers and the two middle fingers, hook them together, with the right pressing over the left.
Bend both thumbs inward into the palms;
with the two ring fingers and the two little fingers,
press down upon the tips of the two thumbs.
With the palms facing inward, recite the Body Mantra at every site of illness and suffering.
For the sake of those who are ill, perform this seal-method;
the illnesses and sufferings of immeasurable sentient beings will all be completely cured.
40. The Seal for Taking Treasures from the Earth. The forty-first [seal] for taking treasures from the earth:
with the four fingers of both hands, cross them respectively in reverse within the palms.
Place both thumbs together pointing downward; by this mudrā, one will know the location where treasures lie beneath the earth.
Having performed this seal:
Recite the body-mantra one hundred and eight times.
Then the deities of the seven treasures will all arrive at once and answer whatever questions are asked. 41.
The Seal for Seeking an Audience with Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, Number Forty-one. With the two ring fingers and little fingers...
Each hand is turned inward with the fingers interlaced, the right pressing down upon the left.
The two middle fingers are held straight and upright with their tips touching each other.
Each of the two index fingers is bent at the second and third joints.
With the two fists turned back-to-back,
press the two thumbs upon the joints of the two index fingers,
and recite the Body Mantra.
Having formed this mudrā,
recite the body-mantra with a sincere heart and focused, right mindfulness.
At that time, Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva will surely manifest his physical form.
Having seen this, the practitioner repents of all their transgressions. 42.
Seeking the Vision of the Buddha’s Seal Mantra, Part Forty-Two. As with the previous seal, perform it as described above.
Change only this: bend the middle finger of the left hand and insert it between the ring finger and the index finger of the right hand;
press the middle finger of the right hand upon the back of the middle finger of the left hand.
The mantra is:
Tadyathā | īri | tīri | svāhā. If one forms this mudrā and recites this mantra, it is as the Master has taught.
When one hundred thousand recitations have been completed,
the Buddhas of the ten directions will come to bestow the prophecy upon the practitioner by touching their crown.
Master Tong said:
The illness persisted for three days up to seven days,
during which time he resolutely sought the method of forming the mudrā.
He was personally graced by [the deity] placing a hand upon his head and bestowing a prophecy.
Thereafter, all dharmas will be accomplished.
While forming this mudrā, fragrant smoke frequently arises. 43.
The Mudrā and Dhāraṇī for Accomplishing All Wishes and Fulfilling the Six Pāramitās, Number Forty-Three. Reverse both hands.
Join the palms with the backs touching;
rotate the wrists outward so that the two thumbs point directly at the eyebrows.
Let it hang downward.
Then, recite the mantra:
*tadyathā* (1) *sarvabuddhāya* (2) *sarvapraśamaya-pratimudraye* (3) *oṃ* (4) *hava hava* (5) *svāhā* (6). *Tadyathā* (7) *mili mili tala* (8) *svāhā* (9). When forming this mudrā:
They give rise to the bodhicitta and universally regard all sentient beings as if they were their own infants.
Having formed this thought, they...
Recite the mantra with a sincere mind until it reaches one hundred thousand recitations.
By the power of this dharma,
all sentient beings shall fully possess the six pāramitās.
Their aspirations will be fulfilled,
and all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, in worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, will all be filled with joy.
44. The Seal of Endowment with All Merits According to the Mind, Number Forty-Four: With the left hand, bend the thumb into the palm.
The remaining four fingers form a fist and are placed under the right armpit;
the right hand is treated in the same manner.
Furthermore, place it under the left armpit;
with the right hand pressing down on the left, recite the Body Mantra.
Once this seal has been formed, while reciting the Body Mantra:
May all immeasurable and boundless sentient beings be fully endowed with all merits. 45.
The Seal of the Mind-Following Ṛddhipāda (The Forty-fifth). First, bend the middle and ring fingers of the left hand into the palm.
Furthermore, press the middle nail of the ring finger with the thumb,
and extend the index and little fingers straight out.
Then, recite the body-mantra.
Having formed this mudrā, rub it upon both feet;
one will travel a thousand li in a single day.
When this mudrā is formed, the Earth Deity constantly receives the practitioner’s feet upon a pedestal of the seven precious jewels;
though those with the fleshly eyes of ordinary beings do not see it,
they give rise to a heart of great compassion and the intent to provide protection.
Do not seek fame, reputation, profit, or offerings for yourself;
you will certainly receive the assistance of the myriad deities. 46.
The Seal for Praying for Wishes According to the Heart (Sui-xin-qi-yuan Yin), the forty-sixth. This seal is used by both masters and dharma-preachers.
Then, with the palms of both hands pressed together side by side,
extend the two little fingers straight upward;
likewise, extend the index, middle, and ring fingers, keeping them pressed against one another.
Place the two ring fingers side by side with their sides touching;
extend the two thumbs and move them back and forth while reciting the Body Mantra.
